findings.conclusion: One known owned writer is created suspended, its HANDLE published atomically before ResumeThread, and retained until the ACK service has joined. The service uses the object signal and actual GetExitCodeThread result rather than a TID or requested exit code. No lookup-by-reused-ID or close-while-waiting. Alive/failed waits do not declare death in the exact mode. This does not register arbitrary foreign workers or prove actual access-denied/query-failure cases.

After a non-cooperative ended writer is detected by a valid ACK request, service atomically sets v4 ABANDONED=7, preserves gate value, and returns explicit abandoned before gate acquisition. Further original calls continue but capture admission remains closed. Repeated ACKs remain responsive. Detection is request-driven; there is an unbounded interval before the next valid ACK. There is no gate recovery or capture restart.

Only this process-owned worker parked at a deliberate event barrier is ended using TerminateThread. Requested success is separated from actual wait signal and code73. All 33 final killed workers have no caller return, no hook finally and no worker finally. Publisher finally begins only in stages9/10. The normal two-path controls have full finally/return counts. Cleanup report explicitly distinguishes cooperative false from resource joins/unmaps; negative false_cleanup is caught.

Seven pre-store barriers cover exact partial reused-slot state, plus after-publication, actual write-AV filter, unwind-before-unlock and after-unlock. Final 12 AVs retain code/operation/PC/address and protections. Publication-stage seq9 is fully published but only observed, not committed; three final endings mark it discarded. Partial slots never enter SQLite.

The target remains live after the worker ends. Ledger correctly refuses source-end reconciliation and stays active during that interval. Only after target process exits does existing reconciliation atomically end the session. Thus abandoned capture while a long-lived target stays alive has no durable terminal cut in this stage; do not infer source death from abandoned, EOF or timeout. All terminal proofs remain same_process_signaled with tail_unknown.

Initial exact implementation without death handling fails after a real code73 thread exit, with ACTIVE/gate1 and no finally. Corrected implementation passes seven representative cases. Two rounds each preserve four failed assertions: omit detection, clear orphan gate, treat living writer as dead, and claim cooperative cleanup. Two builds and all 55 native runs, including nine failures, are immutable; missing-implementation preflight is separate.

Independent script imports no tested modules and checks archived sources/executable, raw thread and process results, receipts-before-ACK, and readonly copies of 55 DB/WAL/SHM sets. Original files unchanged; all 165 child processes exit0, but 47 worker threads were deliberately terminated and are not cooperative cleanup. One offline product run passes382 tests. Controller alive and known fixture barriers are assumptions, not arbitrary TerminateThread/process recovery safety.

In a NEW owned variant, define a bound, durable capture-channel end distinct from target-process death, including receiver restart/replay while target remains alive. Preserve source-end proofs and tail_unknown. Same-slot consumer copy/reuse races, real identity/ABI, arbitrary lifetime/control-page failure, hot unload, CFG/CET and original breakpoint failure remain unproved.
